Fixed.

Just a thought. You are changing the meaning of a protocol field ("sctp.data_tsn" was the absolute seq number and after this patch it will be the relative seq number) and this change is enabled by default.

I don't know the Wireshark policy (if any) about this kind of compatibility across versions, but is that the expected behavior? Just asking, no opinion on that.

The behaviour is the same as for the TCP and DCCP dissectors, so it is consistent with the behaviour of the other dissectors. That is, sctp.data_tsn is relative when the option is on, and absolute if it is off. But there is always the additional field sctp.data_tsn_raw, which contains the raw (i.e. absolute) sequence number. So, if a filter in any case wants absolute sequence numbers, sctp.data_tsn_raw can be used.

For TCP: tcp.seq and tcp.seq_raw; for DCCP: dccp.seq and dccp.seq_raw
Thanks for the explanation, very appreciated

mentioned in issue #17917

This function expects to be passed the raw TSN, not the relative one (and in fact calculates the relative one.)
Having all the entries in the tree off by a fixed value wouldn't matter, except that `ha->first_tsn` is initially set by this function as well, so the first TSN will be passed in as a the raw value, and won't be stored in the tree with the same offset as the others.
Note for the first TSN itself on the first pass, this won't be calculated yet, it's calculated down below.
